title: A council's page listing its candidates' returns of electoral donations and expenses (HTML), each link naming the candidate or the combined file

landmarks: links to files (.pdf, .docx, or a content system's file route) whose words or address say donations, expenses or return
the seat (ward, constituency, mayoralty, community or local board, subdivision, licensing trust) in a heading, accordion title, summary or bold line above the links, or in the link's own words
a link's words name a candidate (more than half of them do not merely say 'View return')

signals_note: Recognised by shape: rows read and their link words name someone (registers/local_elections/load.py shape_of). Northland Regional Council's 2019 and 2025 pages are the first seen (22 October 2026).
notes: The return's file is landed by hash and held, never opened here (ruling 79). A form, a guide, a results notice or a nomination list on the same page is counted by kind, not a row. A link naming a seat, an election or a range and no person is a combined file ('several candidates').
applies_to: councils' returns pages, from the 2019 local election
process: Each file link in document order is an item; the nearest context naming a seat gives the position; the item's words, then the context, then the page's title or address, then the seed give the year.
gates: Every page held is in the ledger (read, followed only, no returns, or set aside).
No row before 2017; a one-candidate row names someone; no value shaped like an email, a phone number or a street address.
on_fail: set the page aside whole; publish nothing check.py holds red

title: A council's election results page whose table or list links each candidate's return with words that name nobody ('View return') (HTML)

landmarks: file links whose words are only 'View return', 'Return', 'PDF', 'Download' or the like, for more than half the returns on the page
the candidate's name in the same table row, list item or paragraph before the link
the seat in the heading above the table

signals_note: Recognised by shape (load.py shape_of); Hutt City's results pages are the kind the survey expects (22 October 2026).
notes: Vote counts in the row are digits and are dropped from the name. The return's file is held, not read.
applies_to: councils' results pages that link returns, from the 2019 local election
process: As council-returns-listing, the name taken from the row's words before the link.

title: A council's elections page, or a folder of its returns, that links no return itself (HTML)

landmarks: no file link the reading calls a return
links on the same host whose words say returns, donations or expenses, or a folder listing's '?path=' links (Tasman's SharePoint folders)

signals_note: A seeded page that yields no row; its sub-listings are followed up to two levels, same host only.
notes: A hub that links nothing the reading follows is 'no returns' in the ledger: either the council publishes none on that page, or it lists them in a shape no profile knows yet (looked at by hand, then carded).
gates: Every page held is in the ledger.

title: A local election candidate's return of electoral donations and expenses (Local Electoral Regulations 2001 Schedule 2 form), or a council's combined file of several, as the council publishes it (PDF, Word, or a scan)

landmarks: the file a council-returns-listing or -results-table row links
the form's title 'Return of electoral donations and expenses' (not checked: the file is not opened)

signals_note: Recognised by the row that links it, never by its contents (ruling 79: no reading).
notes: HELD. The form prints the candidate's and each donor's address (s 112A(4)): when the reading comes it keeps them only in a private twin, never on a view (hard limit 15). Many 2019 and 2022 returns are scans; a combined file holds several candidates. Its reading is its own card, after node1 (ruling 79).
applies_to: returns of the 2019, 2022 and 2025 local elections and the by-elections between
process: Land by hash; record its state on the row that links it.
gates: check.py: a listed return whose page is gone is red.
on_fail: the file's state on its row
